The main takeaway from our work is that
auxiliary splicing signals can be used to predict the outcome of aberrant splice sites.
the relative importance of exon and intron splicing enhancers/silencers in the activation of cryptic splice sites is dependent on the distance between authentic and aberrantly spliced sites.

the splicing machinery has evolved to use the same set of rules to recognize both authentic and aberrant splicing signals, and the relative abundance of auxiliary splicing elements is the main determinant for the selection of authentic or aberrant splicing.
